A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed the first silicon nitride based nonlinear optical devices for the visible spectrum.
the nonlinear optical response of silicon nitride can be exploited to generate visible light using near-infrared light, with applications in optical signal processing and integrated photonic devices.
we have demonstrated second and third harmonic generation from a silicon nitride resonator, and that the phase matching is due to a combination of the χ(2) and χ(3) nonlinearities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the χ(2) and χ(3) susceptibilities of silicon nitride are strong enough to be useful for nonlinear optical processes, and that ring resonators are a promising platform for integrated nonlinear optics.

the χ(2) nonlinearity of Si3N4 can be enhanced by using nanoscale waveguiding structures, and that the second-harmonics generated can be phase-matched to the fundamental waveguide mode using the dispersion of higher-order waveguide modes.
the χ(2) process can be enhanced by a factor of 10(4) in silicon nitride by exploiting the nanoscale geometry of the waveguide and the high-Q ring resonators.
